AddValue's escape removal calls escape_positions.front() right after popping the last element, which is undefined behaviour on an empty queue, and leftover positions leak into later values.

After unifying persistent and transient segments into one tree, InitializeAppend casts data.GetLastSegment() to TransientSegment even when it is a persistent segment loaded by Initialize, so appending after reopening a database hits the assertion or appends into a persistent segment.

The new EncodeDouble special cases encode +inf, -inf and NaN with IEEE-like bit patterns (and a signed 1 << 31 overflow) that do not sort correctly in the ART key order.

PropagateStructExtractStats calls ->Copy() on struct_stats.child_stats[info.index] without checking for null, but StructStatistics can hold null child statistics, causing a null dereference.

defect: The new recursive, dictionary-cursor based ListLoopHash is buggy (it starts with HAS_RSEL ? rsel->get_index(i) : 0 and ignores idata.sel) and still mis-hashes nested lists of lists.

The new ListLoopHash slices the child with a mutable cursor selection and advances it in place (and indexes ldata without the input's selection, with ridx 0 when there is no rsel), which hashes nested lists of lists inconsistently.

MapExtractBind now takes value_type = child_types[1].second, the LIST type of the map's values, instead of its child type, so map_extract's return type becomes a list of lists and the bind data carries the wrong type.
MapExtractBind now uses child_types[1].second (the LIST of values) as value_type instead of its child type, so map_extract returns LIST(LIST(value)).

fix_subject: Fix data race on exceptions in executor
defect: The new in-loop check 'if (!exceptions.empty())' and 'throw Exception(exceptions[0])' read the shared exceptions vector without executor_lock while other threads push errors into it, which is a data race.
The new in-loop check reads the shared exceptions vector (empty() and exceptions[0]) without holding the executor lock while worker threads push errors into it under that lock, a data race.

The FullScanHashTable moved into the executor comments out FillSelectionVectorSwitch, so sel_build and sel_addresses are passed to Gather uninitialized.

Replacing cached_chunk.Reset() with SetCardinality(0) keeps the cached chunk's validity masks from earlier appends, so stale NULLs leak into later cached join output (#2102).

fix_subject: fixing a pretty evil nested type reading bug in the parquet reader
defect: ListColumnReader::Read calls child_result.Reset() at the start of every call, which resets data[1] (the overflow slice kept for the next call) to its cache buffer, so list child values spilling over a Read boundary are lost, and data[0] is reused across loop iterations.

The change counts probe matches in the member probe_sel_count of the PerfectHashJoinExecutor, which is shared by all threads probing the join and is never reset, so the count races and accumulates across chunks.

ExecutePull now runs in RunFunctionInTryCatch, which turns exceptions into executor.PushError and returns an empty chunk, and on interrupt it silently returns; Executor::FetchChunk never checks the pushed error, so pull-mode errors and interrupts end as silently truncated results.

fix_subject: Fix #3349: correctly handle empty table case in grouping set

The empty-input special case in GetData was rekeyed from is_implicit_aggr to grouping_set.empty() but still asserts the output chunk holds only aggregates and writes aggregates[i] into chunk.data[i], which is wrong (assert or out-of-bounds/misplaced columns) for an empty grouping set inside GROUPING SETS where the chunk also carries the group columns that must be NULL.

The new even() rounds incorrectly: for FLOAT/DOUBLE the check ceil(x) / 2 * 2 == ceil(x) is always true in floating point, so odd values are returned unchanged, and negative inputs are not rounded away from zero in the integral and decimal variants.

defect: round_info.should_round uses 'digit <= -5' for negative numbers although digit is uint8_t, so negative decimals are never rounded.
should_round is computed as NEGATIVE ? digit <= -5 : digit >= 5 with an unsigned digit 0..9, so it is always false for negative inputs and negative decimals are never rounded.
On a metadata-cache hit HTTPFileHandle::Initialize returns early before allocating read_buffer (returning a null response), so later reads use a null buffer.
On a metadata-cache hit HTTPFileHandle::Initialize returns early before read_buffer is allocated, so later reads use a null buffer.

fix_subject: Fix for dtypes when combined with union by name
defect: The new COLUMN_TYPES check in SniffCSV throws a BinderException whenever a named column is missing from the file being sniffed, which breaks union_by_name, where each per-file reader is sniffed with the same options and files may lack some columns.
The new COLUMN_TYPES handling throws when a named column is missing from a file, which breaks union_by_name reads where a column exists only in some files.
The union tag is read as int8_t although tags are uint8_t, so tags of 128 and above become negative and never match their member index.

CreateValuesUnion reads the union tag as int8_t although union_tag_t is uint8_t and unions allow up to 256 members, so tags of 128 and above become negative and never match member_idx (and the comparison mixes signedness).

fix_subject: Fix performance regression in read_csv_auto auto detection
defect: Dialect detection now parses up to sample_chunks buffers for every quote/delimiter/escape candidate, multiplying sniffing cost and causing a large read_csv_auto performance regression.

Dialect sniffing now calls TryParseCSV up to sample_chunks times per candidate; after the first call sniffed_column_counts already exceeds the == sample_chunk_size stop check, so each further call parses on through the file for every dialect candidate, a large auto-detect performance regression.

The new PythonFilesystem declares OpenFile and Read with the glibc-internal types __uint8_t and __int64_t instead of uint8_t and int64_t, which do not exist on MSVC, so the Python package fails to compile on Windows.
The overrides use glibc-internal typedefs __uint8_t and __int64_t instead of uint8_t and int64_t, which do not exist on other toolchains such as MSVC, breaking the Python package build there.

fix_subject: fixed bug that caused the ManagedSelection to have a size of 1, leading to an issue in foreign key append verification
defect: The new default ManagedSelection() leaves size 0 and is only lazily initialized, so a ConflictManager that records no conflicts returns a selection whose Size() does not match the input, breaking FirstMissingMatch and foreign-key append verification.

The new default ManagedSelection() leaves size at 0 while uninitialized, so a foreign key check with no matches yields an empty selection and FirstMissingMatch, which iterates Size(), cannot find the missing row.

fix_subject: fixed bug that caused the ManagedSelection to have a size of 1, leading to an issue in foreign key append verification
defect: The constructor now defaults the mode to THROW and ShouldThrow returns true for every hit when no conflicts were scanned, so foreign-key append verification, which never switches to SCAN, throws a constraint error on valid inserts.

ConflictManager now defaults to THROW mode and ShouldThrow returns true when no conflict set exists, so foreign key verification, which passes a ConflictInfo and expects hits to be recorded, throws on every matching key.

fix_subject: fix CI failure on empty quote, and fix typo
defect: The new SetQuote silently ignores an empty quote string, where the previous code set quote='' and has_quote, so QUOTE '' no longer disables quoting.
The new SetQuote returns early on an empty string, so a user-specified empty QUOTE is ignored and has_quote stays false, whereas the old code set quote to empty and marked it as set.

JSONGlobalTableFunctionState::Init returns a unique_ptr<JSONGlobalTableFunctionState> lvalue as unique_ptr<GlobalTableFunctionState> without std::move, which does not compile on gcc 4.8 (no implicit move to a converted type).
JSONGlobalTableFunctionState::Init returns a unique_ptr<JSONGlobalTableFunctionState> as unique_ptr<GlobalTableFunctionState> without std::move, which does not compile on GCC 4.8.

fix_subject: Fix #7659 - and disable checkpoint on shutdown when ALTERNATE_VERIFY is enabled
defect: ReplayCreateType checks Catalog::TypeExists with info->catalog, which is never deserialized (empty), so it looks in the default or search-path catalog rather than the database being replayed; replaying into an attached database then creates the type twice and fails.

ReplayCreateType now skips creation only if Catalog::TypeExists finds the type via the context's default catalog (info->catalog is empty), so replaying an attached database looks in the wrong catalog and recreates or skips types incorrectly.

EliminateCandidateFormats is declared void and prunes the shared DateFormatMap format list, so a non-date string field pops every format and the caller infers failure from an empty list, breaking date/timestamp detection for other fields.

EliminateCandidateFormats (void, popping failed formats from the shared DateFormatMap) empties the format list for all JSON fields as soon as one field fails to parse, so date/timestamp detection fails for later fields.

fix_subject: fix: logic fix to allow storage extension to implement DROP DATABASE
defect: The rewritten loop skips extensions whose drop_database is set (continue on != nullptr) and calls drop_database on extensions where it is null.

The rewritten loop skips storage extensions that have drop_database and calls the null drop_database of the others; the removed break also makes DROP DATABASE fall through to the default case that throws.

fix_subject: fix deadlock when doing scan resets
defect: The change closes the JSON file right after reading the last buffer via CloseJSONFile, which spins until requested_reads equals actual_reads; reads served from the cache never bump actual_reads and Reset never clears the counters, so scans after a reset spin forever (deadlock).

The change closes a JSON file right after its last buffer via CloseJSONFile, which spins until requested_reads == actual_reads, but the counters it added are never incremented on the cached-read path and never reset by Reset, so a scan reset deadlocks.

fix_subject: fix: swap RemoveDirectory impl to use rm with recursive
defect: The new RemoveDirectory calls fsspec rmdir, which only removes empty directories, whereas DuckDB's RemoveDirectory contract is a recursive removal.
The new PythonFilesystem::RemoveDirectory calls fsspec rmdir, which only removes empty directories, while DuckDB's RemoveDirectory contract is a recursive removal.

fix_subject: Fix for joining on pivot statements
defect: Enum names were changed from a UUID to __pivot_enum_<pivot_entries.size()>_<c>, but in a child transformer the entries go to the parent, so the local count stays 0 and several pivots (e.g. in a join) get the same enum name, the later one replacing the earlier.

Pivot enum names are built from the local pivot_entries.size(), but AddPivotEntry forwards entries to the parent transformer, so in child transformers the count stays 0 and two pivots get the same enum name, which REPLACE_ON_CONFLICT then silently overwrites.

fix_subject: Fix for joining on pivot statements
defect: The PIVOT check was added only in TransformSelect, so pivots reached through TransformSelectNode directly (set operations, COPY, SHOW) are transformed as ordinary selects and the pivot is ignored.
The new PIVOT select form is only handled in TransformSelect, while subqueries, joins and set operations call TransformSelectNode directly and so transform a pivot SelectStmt as an ordinary select.
has_result is computed as return_type == StatementReturnType::NOTHING, the inverse of its meaning, so statements without results are chained and those with results are dropped.
has_result is computed as return_type == StatementReturnType::NOTHING, the inverse of its meaning, so result chaining keeps the results of the wrong statements.

vdata.validity.SetAllValid(count) allocates a mask for STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE rows and writes count bits, which overflows the buffer when a nested list child column is appended with more than STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE elements.

defect: LCMOperator returns left * (right / gcd) without taking the absolute value, so lcm with a negative argument gives a negative result.
LCMOperator returns left * (right / gcd) with its sign, so lcm of a negative and a positive input is negative instead of the non-negative least common multiple.

The new AllNewLine helper returns true for an empty value, so the final empty value of a single-column CSV (a NULL row, e.g. an empty quoted value at EOF) is silently dropped instead of added.
The new AllNewLine helper returns true for an empty value, so at the end of the file an empty (e.g. quoted empty) last value of a single-column CSV is skipped instead of being added as a row.

defect: PandasColumn stores the result of getter(names[index]) as a non-owning py::handle, so when the column object is created on access, its temporary py::object is freed and the handle dangles.

PandasDataFrame::operator[] stores the owning result of getter(names[index]) in PandasColumn's non-owning py::handle, so the column object can be freed when operator[] returns and BindColumn then uses a dangling handle.

Join key columns are compressed with each side's own statistics and only the compressed types are compared, so the two sides can be shifted by different minima (and a null compress expression is dereferenced), giving wrong join comparisons.

Join condition columns are left to be compressed generically when each side's own-statistics compress expression has the same return type, but each side is compressed with different statistics (different offsets), so equality comparisons in the join go wrong; it also dereferences a possibly null GetCompressExpression result.

CTENode::ToString prints only the parenthesized CTE query and drops the child (main) query, so the generated SQL is wrong and breaks the ToString round-trip.

fix_subject: fix issue caused by consuming unnamed values in PrepareParameters
defect: PrepareParameters takes the unnamed values by value and returns them by move, and its caller passes std::move(unnamed_values), so the caller's parameter vector is consumed and re-executing a prepared statement sees empty values.
PrepareParameters takes the unnamed values by value and the callers std::move the caller's vector and stmt.values into it, consuming parameters that are needed again (re-execution, rebinding).

BoundCTENode::GetRootIndex returns setop_index, although the node's output columns are those of its child, so callers bind to a table index that does not produce the result.

The new resumable sink-interrupt handling only re-sinks final_chunk after a BLOCKED result, so pending HAVE_MORE_OUTPUT work in intermediate operators or in a flush step is dropped or reprocessed on resume.

The new interrupted_while_flushing flag records any sink block during flushing, so on resume the cached chunk is re-pushed even when nothing was pending (duplicate rows) or after flushing_idx already advanced (wrong chunk).

The early return checks get.table_filters.filters.empty() instead of !empty(), so filter pushdown into a GET is skipped exactly when no filters were pushed yet (and the pending filters are dropped).

fix_subject: Fixes, via code duplication, problems with recent gcc compilers
defect: The change declares template FillFunctionDescriptions here and calls it, relying on an implicit instantiation emitted in another translation unit (register_function_list.cpp), which recent gcc does not export, causing a link failure.

The extension declares the template FillFunctionDescriptions but relies on a definition in register_function_list.cpp that is never explicitly instantiated for this translation unit, so linking fails with recent GCC.

fix_subject: Fix for >2 layers deeply nested structs
defect: HandleStructExtractRecursive, declared here with one ColumnIndex out-parameter, builds the index by AddChildIndex at each level, so for more than two nested struct levels the deeper fields become siblings instead of nested children.

HandleStructExtractRecursive builds a single ColumnIndex by AddChildIndex on the top-level index, so for more than two nested struct_extract levels the deeper field becomes a sibling instead of a grandchild and the wrong sub-fields are projected.

defect: The added 'cursor.reset(nullptr)' lacks a semicolon (and passes nullptr to shared_ptr::reset), so the Python extension does not compile.
cursor.reset(nullptr) lacks its terminating semicolon (and reset(nullptr) is the wrong overload), so the Python package fails to compile.

fix_subject: fix log level enum conflict with windows macro
defect: This change introduces the LogLevel enumerator ERROR (and its EnumUtil mapping), which collides with the ERROR macro from windows.h and breaks Windows compilation.
The change adds LogLevel::ERROR, which collides with the ERROR macro from windows.h and breaks compilation on Windows.
Adds the internal header as #include <duckdb/optimizer/optimizer.hpp> with angle brackets, which the amalgamation script (which only inlines quoted includes) leaves as an unresolved include.
The added angle-bracket include <duckdb/optimizer/optimizer.hpp> is not inlined by scripts/amalgamation.py, so the amalgamation build (compiled with only -Isrc/amalgamation) cannot find it.

The new guard in Normalize tests 'done > 0.0' before dividing by total instead of 'total > 0.0', so total == 0 with done > 0 divides by zero, and ProgressDone, whose clamping this change removed, now returns inf.
The rewritten Normalize guards the division with done > 0.0 instead of total > 0.0, so a zero total still divides by zero when done is positive and a negative done is left unnormalised.
The re-enabled macOS block tests flags & FileFlags::FILE_FLAGS_DIRECT_IO, but FileOpenFlags has no operator&, so the file does not compile on macOS.
The re-enabled macOS block tests flags & FileFlags::FILE_FLAGS_DIRECT_IO, but FileOpenFlags has no operator&, so the file does not compile on macOS.

LogStorageScanState is used polymorphically through unique_ptr<LogStorageScanState> (and DynamicCastCheck) but has no virtual destructor, so deleting an InMemoryLogStorageScanState is undefined behaviour and skips its ColumnDataScanState destructor.

LogStorageScanState has no virtual destructor (and is not polymorphic for DynamicCastCheck) although InMemoryLogStorageScanState, holding a ColumnDataScanState, is owned and deleted through unique_ptr<LogStorageScanState>.
The new ScanToDictionaryVector declares 'auto result_data = FlatVector::GetData<string_t>(result)' and never uses it, an unused variable that fails the warnings-as-errors build.
ScanToDictionaryVector declares 'result_data' and never uses it, which breaks the warnings-as-errors build.

The new finalize condition requires ht.Count() < PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD && skew > SKEW_SINGLE_THREADED_THRESHOLD, so large skewed builds still finalize in parallel (the case the change meant to fix) and small unskewed builds lose their single-threaded finalize.
The single-threaded-finalize condition requires a small HT AND high skew, so small HTs now go parallel and large skewed HTs still slam the same atomics, the opposite of the stated intent.

For NULL constants in OR filters, IS DISTINCT FROM NULL is mapped to IsNullFilter and IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL to IsNotNullFilter (inverted), and = NULL / <> NULL push null filters although they never match.

When an OR child compares a column with a NULL constant the change pushes IsNullFilter for IS DISTINCT FROM NULL and IsNotNullFilter for IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL (and also maps = NULL / <> NULL), which is the inverse of the SQL semantics and lets the zone-map filter prune row groups that contain matching rows.

fix_subject: fix windows ci failure file url
defect: On Windows, PathSeparator only treats the prefix 'file:/' as a URL, so joining onto 'file:' (how the change's own no-host test builds its URLs) yields a backslash separator and the new file:/ tests fail on Windows.

On Windows, PathSeparator was changed to recognise only the file:/ prefix, so JoinPath with a bare file: base (as the commit's new no-host test builds it) inserts a backslash and yields an unrecognised file:-backslash URL, failing the Windows build of the commit's own test.
The BinderException check was replaced by the inverted D_ASSERT(children.size() != 1), which fires for every valid single-child NOT in debug builds.
The new D_ASSERT(children.size() != 1) is inverted, so every valid NOT expression fails the assertion in debug builds.

When the IN filter is pushed, Finalize now skips the min/max range filters, although the IN filter is an OptionalFilter used only for zonemap pruning, so probe-side scans lose their real filtering (performance regression).
When an IN filter is pushed, Finalize now skips the min/max range filters, leaving only an OptionalFilter used for zonemap pruning, so probe-side scans lose their filtering, a performance regression.

The regenerated enum util adds ToChars/FromString for DictionaryAppendState as duckdb::DictionaryAppendState, but the enum lives in duckdb::dict_fsst, so DictionaryAppendState::REGULAR etc. do not compile.

The generated enum util code declares and uses duckdb::DictionaryAppendState, but the enum lives in namespace duckdb::dict_fsst, so DictionaryAppendState::REGULAR etc. do not resolve and the build fails.

The commit registers the 'recurring.<cte>' CTE reference only in the right binder but makes bind_basetableref look up cte_references['recurring.<cte>'], so referencing recurring.tbl from another CTE of a MATERIALIZED USING KEY CTE dereferences a null shared_ptr.

The change adds a recurring.<cte> CTE binding only inside the recursive part and, in bind_basetableref.cpp, looks up cte_references by "recurring.<name>", so a reference to recurring.tbl from another (materialized) CTE dereferences a null shared_ptr.

fix_subject: add escape tests for maps, also fix a bug: map keys are allowed to be empty, should accept this in cast
defect: The rewritten SplitStringMapInternal returns false when a map key is empty ('Key can not be empty'), so casts of maps with empty keys now fail.
The rewritten SplitStringMapInternal returns false when a map key is empty ('Key can not be empty'), so casts like '{=1}' that the old FindKeyOrValueMap accepted now fail.

WKBColumnWriterState was declared with ParquetCastOperator while WKBColumnWriter uses ParquetStringOperator, so StandardColumnWriter casts the state to a different template instantiation (failed dynamic cast check / type punning).

WKBColumnWriterState was changed to StandardColumnWriterState<string_t, string_t, ParquetCastOperator> while WKBColumnWriter is a StandardColumnWriter with ParquetStringOperator, so the writer casts its state to the wrong template subclass.

When copying from a partially overlapping cached range, Read neither advances current_location and remaining_bytes after the memcpy nor recomputes buffer_offset after reading the gap, so later reads write at wrong offsets and re-read bytes.

When combining overlapping cached ranges, Read computes buffer_offset before the gap read and never advances current_location/remaining_bytes after memcpy, so data lands at wrong offsets and is re-read.
In the filter path the result vector is indexed with the file column id (reader_data.column_ids[id]) instead of the local position id, so filtered columns are read into the wrong output vector.

In the filter path the result vector is chosen with result.data[local_col_id] (the file column id) instead of the output position id, while the other two loops in the same change use the output index.

The new TableFunctionRef::ToString appends WITH ORDINALITY after BaseToString has already added the alias and column aliases (giving func() AS t(a) WITH ORDINALITY, which does not re-parse), and as committed it even lacks a return statement.
ToString appends ' WITH ORDINALITY' after BaseToString has already added the alias (and originally had no return statement), producing unparsable 'f() AS t(a) WITH ORDINALITY'.
VerifyBuffers is added as a pure virtual method of BoundIndex, so extension index types that subclass BoundIndex become abstract and the extension build breaks.
VerifyBuffers is added as a pure virtual to BoundIndex, so index types in extensions that derive from it and do not implement it become abstract and fail to build.

IsTriviallyMappable returns true for leaf columns before checking the expected child position and type, so structs with reordered or retyped fields are treated as trivially mappable and skip remap_struct, giving wrong results.

IsTriviallyMappable returns true for any found leaf column before checking expected_idx and the type, so reordered or retyped struct children (and retyped top-level columns) are treated as trivially mappable, skipping remap_struct and filter casts.

The new occupancy estimate multiplies distinct counts of group columns across all grouping sets, so with GROUPING SETS/CUBE the product explodes (to inf), the 1-exp term becomes 0 and the estimate degenerates to 0 or NaN.

defect: After state became a raw pointer, operator= still asserts RefersToSameObject(state, other.state), which compares the addresses of the two pointer members and fails for every non-self assignment (and does not allow a null default-constructed state).

The new branch-free Subtract mishandles wrap-around when (value - tuple_idx) is a multiple of the block size, leaving tuple_idx equal to the divisor and block_idx one too low.

The new branch-free Subtract borrows div + 1 blocks with div = floor(deficit / divisor), so when the deficit is an exact multiple of the block size tuple_idx ends equal to the divisor (out of range) and block_idx is off by one.

The new can_add check looks up projection output bindings (projection.table_index, idx) in a distinct group made of the child's bindings, so it never matches and distinct groups never propagate through projections (e.g. joins on GROUP BY subqueries are no longer eliminated, failing the PR's own test).
The added DEBUG block asserts that the projection's own bindings belong to the referenced table's distinct group, which can never hold, so debug builds hit an assertion whenever the sizes differ.

The added DEBUG block asserts that every projection binding in columns_idx lies in distinct_group, but columns_idx holds bindings with the projection's table index, so in debug builds the assertion fails whenever a projection references only part of a distinct group.

The cache map stores std::promise objects, so every lookup calls get_future() again (future_already_retrieved) and blocks under the cache lock.

GetInstanceInternal can return nullptr after releasing the cache lock (shutdown path), yet GetOrCreateInstance then passes the unlocked lock to CreateInstanceInternal, which unlocks it again and touches db_instances unlocked.

OFFSET_SIZE_MINUS_ONE_SHIFT is 5, but the variant metadata header stores offset_size_minus_one in bits 6-7, so the offset size is decoded wrongly.

BindCopyOptions binds every option expression, but a bare * (for example FORCE_QUOTE *), which the old grammar turned into a '*' string, now becomes a StarExpression that cannot be bound, so a previously supported COPY option breaks.

Node4::DeleteChild marks the freed node as LEAF_INLINED before Prefix::Concat; when prefix aliases node (no prefix above), Concat receives a leaf as parent and violates its D_ASSERT(!parent.IsAnyLeaf()).

ConvertVariantToValue indexes the VARIANT blob data with value_data[row] instead of value_data[value.sel->get_index(row)], reading the wrong blob (or out of bounds) for dictionary or constant input vectors.

The new null-skip and validity asserts in VariantUtils::Verify index the unified formats with the raw sel_p index instead of mapping through each format's selection vector, so dictionary inputs check and read the wrong rows.

Every column not used as key or aggregate gets a LAST payload aggregate even for recursive CTEs without USING KEY, so plain recursive CTEs acquire payload aggregates that alter their resolved types and bindings.
Every column not used as a key or aggregate gets a LAST aggregate unconditionally, also for ordinary recursive CTEs without USING KEY, which changes their planning and semantics.

The new WAL/database mismatch checks in ReplayVersion throw SerializationException, which WAL replay treats as a torn WAL and silently ignores, so a mismatched WAL is skipped instead of reported.

The new verification in FinalizeCheckpoint throws an InternalException when new segment starts do not chain from col_data.start, which the author found to be an incorrect invariant.

The new bloom filter pushdown is gated on join_condition.size() == 1 (pushdown-eligible conditions) instead of the hash table's condition count, and it always filters NULLs, so for multi-key hash tables or NULL-equal joins it can drop matching rows.

HashInternal hashes with the selection vector, which writes hashes at the selected row indices into a vector sized approved_tuple_count (out of bounds) while LookupHashes reads the dense positions 0..count, giving crashes and wrong filter results.

BloomFilterState allocates hashes_v, keys_flat_v and bf_sel with a fixed STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE capacity while Filter writes approved_tuple_count entries into them, overflowing when the count exceeds that capacity.

This commit makes the scan state hold a shared_ptr to the DatabaseInstance, declared as the last member of ColumnDataScanState, so it is destroyed before the pinned chunk handles, which then unpin against a possibly freed database (use-after-free).

The change adds shared_ptr<DatabaseInstance> db to ColumnDataScanState as its last member and assigns it after clearing handles, so the database can be released before the scan's BufferHandles are destroyed.

The row_limit logic declared here (AddRowGroupWithLimit) counts overlapping row groups as qualifying (second clause lacks the stat_type check, every overlap adds one), so the reorderer can stop before row groups that hold top-N rows and ORDER BY ... LIMIT returns wrong rows.
use_limit enables row-group pruning by row count even when an aggregate sits between the Top-N and the scan or an order is NULLS FIRST, so row groups that hold result rows can be skipped.

fix_subject: Refactor `struct_keys` to replace `dict_child` with `keys_vector` for clarity and consistency, fixed a bug when the input is a constant vector
defect: For constant input the result Reference()s the bind data's shared keys vector and is retyped as CONSTANT, so later operations on the result (e.g. Flatten moving the auxiliary list child out of the shared buffer) corrupt the bind data used by later calls.

For constant input the change returns result.Reference(dict_child) turned into a CONSTANT_VECTOR, so the result shares the bind data's list-entry and validity buffers in which row 1 is marked NULL; Vector::Flatten of a non-null constant keeps that validity, so row 1 becomes NULL, and writes to the result would corrupt the shared bind data.

fix_subject: Fix bug with like not respective correct order
defect: LikeClause now parses its right-hand side as a full Expression instead of OtherOperatorExpression, so LIKE binds looser than AND, OR and comparisons and swallows the rest of the expression.
LikeClause now takes a full Expression as its pattern operand, so lower-precedence operators (e.g. AND) are swallowed into the LIKE pattern and expressions parse with the wrong precedence.

fix_subject: fix virtual columns and projection ids
defect: In the new projection_ids branch the column map is keyed by the loop counter col_idx, but LogicalGet column bindings use the projection id itself, so columns of GETs with non-trivial projection_ids are mapped to the wrong canonical indices.

With projection_ids present, the column map is keyed by position in the projection list, but LogicalGet::GetColumnBindings uses the projection id itself as the column index, so bindings map to the wrong columns (and the virtual-column bail-out runs after projection_ids were already moved out).
